We strive to cultivate lifelong learning by offering high-quality undergraduate and graduate programs with a technological emphasis. We lead our students in developing cutting-edge skills to make informed decisions, uphold ethical standards, thrive in their careers, and contribute to society. The Department of Accounting emphasizes immersive, technology-rich education tailored to modern business complexity. Its culture is grounded in experiential learning, ethical decision-making, and analytical rigor. Through simulations, case analyses, and software-integrated coursework, students are trained to support organizational accountability in public, private, governmental, and nonprofit sectors. Faculty bring real-world professional and scholarly experience, contributing to the department’s reputation as a regional leader in applied accounting education. Students benefit from accessible accounting analytics labs, collaborative workspaces with audit-case simulations, and access to emerging technologies. The Accounting Society and Beta Alpha Psi chapter offer networking, community outreach, and participation in national competitions. Structured internships, peer mentorship programs, and tech-focused workshops help students build career-ready competencies. courses.title: Financial Accounting for Decision Making
courses.description: Introduction to financial accounting and accounting information systems (AIS), including basic concepts, limitations, tools and methods, use of AIS-generated information, including financial statements in decision making by investors, creditors, and other users external to the organization.
courses.prerequisites: CIS 101, CIS 1010 , or PCPT.

courses.title: Managerial Accounting for Decision Making
courses.description: Introduction to managerial accounting and accounting information systems (AIS), including basic concepts, limitations, tools and methods. Use of AIS-generated information to support the internal decision-making functions of an organization. For credit, both segments are to be successfully completed.
courses.prerequisites: ACC 2070 ; or ACC 207 and ACC 207A.

courses.title: Intermediate Accounting I
courses.description: Fundamental financial accounting concepts that underlie U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) and international financial reporting systems (IFRS), and their application to the basic financial statements, revenue recognition, fair-value accounting and assets.
courses.prerequisites: Accounting option/major/minor/certificate and C or better in ACC 2070 or ACC 207/ACC 207A; ACC 2080 or ACC 208/ACC 208A; EC 2201 or EC 201; EC 2202 or EC 202; GE Area 1A/A2; FRL 2013 or FRL 201; MAT 1250 or MAT 125, MAT 114 and MAT 115, or MAT 1140 ; and STA 1200 , STA 1202 , or STA 120.

courses.title: Intermediate Accounting II
courses.description: Fundamental financial accounting concepts that underlie U.S. GAAP and IFRS, and their application to liabilities, equity, and special topics including income taxes, leases, pensions, share-based compensation, EPS, accounting changes, error corrections, and cash flows statement. *The enforcement of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement has been temporarily suspended per a Chancellor’s Office memorandum.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3110 , or ACC 311 and ACC 312; and GWT*, CPU 4010 *, or CPU 401*.

courses.title: Cost Accounting
courses.description: Accounting information for management of all types of business entities including cost concepts; cost accumulation and analysis; product costing; master and flexible budgeting; standard costing and variance analysis; responsibility accounting; decision making and relevant information; and pricing decisions and analysis.
courses.prerequisites: Accounting option/major/minor/certificate and C or better in ACC 2070 or ACC 207/ACC 207A; ACC 2080 or ACC 208/ACC 208A; EC 2201 or EC 201; EC 2202 or EC 202; GE Area 1A/A2; FRL 2013 or FRL 201; MAT 1250 or MAT 125, MAT 114 and MAT 115, or MAT 1140 ; and STA 1200 , STA 1202 , or STA 120.

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Financial Accounting and Analysis
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ACC 5122 Understanding essential financial accounting standards (U.S. GAAP and IFRS) and FASB Conceptual Framework from both preparer’s and user’s perspectives.
courses.prerequisites: Not an ACCT major and C or better in ACC 2070 or ACC 207/ACC 207A; ACC 2080 or ACC 208/ACC 208A; EC 2201 or EC 201; EC 2202 or EC 202; FRL 2013 or FRL 201; MAT 1250 or MAT 125; and CIS 101, CIS 1010 , or PCPT.

courses.title: Advanced Financial Accounting
courses.description: Advanced financial accounting topics in corporation and partnership accounting including consolidations, derivatives of financial instruments, foreign currency transactions and translation, interim reporting and disclosures.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3120 or ACC 313.

courses.title: Advanced Cost Accounting
courses.description: Advanced cost accounting techniques focusing on activity-based-costing; cost allocation issues and customer profitability; service department cost allocations; accounting for spoilage, rework, and scrap; inventory costing and management; cost behavior; transfer pricing; divisional performance measurement; and capital budgeting.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3210 or ACC 307.

courses.title: Controllership
courses.description: Supervision and dissemination of financial and managerial information, taxation, and any other required reporting to diverse users, including management, stockholders, creditors (e.g., banks and suppliers), stock exchanges, employees, customers, U.S. government agencies (e.g., the Securities and Exchange Commission, Internal Revenue Service, Department of Commerce, Department of Labor, and the Federal Trade Commission), and state and other agencies.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3110 , or ACC 311 and ACC 312; and C or better in ACC 3210 or ACC 307.

courses.title: Introduction to Taxation
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ACC 5310 Fundamental principles of income taxation leading to the preparation of federal tax and state returns, including tax determination, gross income, deductions, property transactions, depreciation, employee expenses, self-employed deductions and Passive Activity Losses. Course emphasizes written and oral communication skills and tax research. *The enforcement of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement has been temporarily suspended per a Chancellor’s Office memorandum.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3110 , or ACC 311 and ACC 312; and GWT*, CPU 4010 *, or CPU 401*.

courses.title: Advanced Taxation
courses.description: Federal and international taxation of legal entities (corporations, partnerships, fiduciaries, tax-exempt organizations), including credits; accounting methods and periods; organization and applicable taxation concepts of these entities. Course emphasizes development of written and oral communication skills, tax research and tax return preparation.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 4310 or ACC 431.

courses.title: Tax Procedure and Research
courses.description: Procedural aspects of dealing with the Internal Revenue Service, including administration procedures governing tax controversies; rights and obligations of taxpayers and tax practitioners. Coverage of tax research methodology, including case studies, and communication of research results.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 4310 or ACC 431.

courses.title: Service Learning in Taxation
courses.description: Federal and state individual income tax-return preparation for elderly and low-income taxpayers at supervised sites, such as through the IRS Voluntary Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program. Provides students with an introduction to procedural steps of dealing with the IRS.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor Consent.

courses.title: Supervisory Service Learning in Taxation
courses.description: Emphasis on the supervisory role in the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance program (return-preparation). Involvement in assisting student tax preparers and taxpayers with ‘real world’ tax preparation issues providing a diverse learning experience.
courses.prerequisites: ACC 4341 and Instructor Consent.

courses.title: Service Learning in Taxation - LITC
courses.description: Quality experiential learning experience in the field of taxation as clinicians representing low-income taxpayers in our community. Assist taxpayers in IRS examination and collection matters, including audits, offers-in-compromise, penalty abatements, innocent spouse claims, appeals, Tax Court cases, etc. Provide community outreach and education regarding tax obligations and benefits to persons with limited English proficiency.
courses.prerequisites: ACC 4310 and consent of instructor. Pre or Corequisite(s): ACC 4331 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units, with a maximum of 2 units per semester.

courses.title: Accounting Internship
courses.description: On-the-job training in accounting involving new university-level learning experiences. Experiences may be useful as a basis for senior projects. Maximum of 3 units of Career Emphasis may be satisfied by internship.
courses.prerequisites: Director of Internship Program consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 3 units.

courses.title: Internship in Public Accounting
courses.description: On-the-job training with a CPA firm in phases of auditing or public accounting. The experience must be new to the student. Analytical reports of work accomplished by each student are made periodically to the faculty coordinator. Units of college credit granted are dependent on departmental approval. Maximum of 3 units of Career Emphasis may be satisfied by internship.
courses.prerequisites: Director of Internship Program consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken only once Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 1 - 3 units each.

courses.title: Accounting Information Systems
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ACC 5510 Role, design, implementation, and management of the accounting information system as a subset of the management information system. Interface between accountants and computer specialists. Short case studies. *The enforcement of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement has been temporarily suspended per a Chancellor’s Office memorandum.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3110 or ACC 311; and GWT*, CPU 4010 *, or CPU 401*.

courses.title: Analytics in Accounting
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ACC 5530 Analysis of data as it pertains to Accountants. Focuses on analytic techniques for decision making and examination of “big data” involving accounting information. Hands-on experience to develop skills with select software tools used in data analytics for accounting professionals.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3120 or ACC 313; ACC 3210 or ACC 307; ACC 4310 or ACC 431; ACC 4510 or ACC 304; ACC 4810 or ACC 419; CIS 3100 or CIS 310.

courses.title: Professional Accounting Communication
courses.description: Study of professionalism and communication skills necessary in the field of accounting through individual and team assignments including case studies. Application of effective oral and written communication skills. Assignments include written pieces required in the profession of accounting, such as memos, emails, disclosures, research paper, and interviews. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing, and C or better in ACC 3110 .

courses.title: Senior Project I
courses.description: Familiarization with sources of data and academic literature for research-oriented projects: problem identification and analysis, research methodology, application of report writing tools and techniques under the faculty supervision. Project(s) must involve research and/or field study and formal writing.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3110 ; or ACC 311 and ACC 312.

courses.title: Governmental and Not-for-Profit Accounting
courses.description: Budgetary and fund accounting as applied to municipalities, other governmental units, and institutions operating as not-for-profit entities
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3110 ; or ACC 311 and ACC 312.

courses.title: Auditing
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ACC 5810 Auditing standards and procedures used by assurance auditors including types of audit reports; internal controls; audit evidence; professional responsibilities and legal liabilities; and standards of reporting financial information. *The enforcement of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement has been temporarily suspended per a Chancellor’s Office memorandum.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3110 , or ACC 311 and ACC 312; C or better in TOM 3020 or TOM 302; and GWT*, CPU 4010 *, or CPU 401*.

courses.title: Accounting Ethics
courses.description: Importance of ethics in accounting practice; frameworks for ethical decision making; professional codes of ethics in accounting; ethical use of Artificial Intelligence technology; and current and classic ethics cases. Assignments include written pieces required in the profession of accounting, such as memos, emails, disclosures, and research papers. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing, and C or better in ACC 3110 .

courses.title: Forensic Accounting
courses.description: Study of forensic accounting, a discipline that focuses on the procedures and techniques used in the prevention, investigation, and detection of occupational and financial statement fraud. Study of social, ethical, legal, and political considerations that surround fraud.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3110 ; or ACC 311 and ACC 312.

courses.title: Advanced Auditing
courses.description: Application of auditing procedures and techniques; working paper development and preparation; use of computer auditing tools; and extensive case analysis.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 4810 or ACC 419.

courses.title: Internal Auditing
courses.description: Objectives, principles and methods of internal and operational auditing with special emphasis on examination and appraisal of internal controls in operations and reporting systems; problems of communication, delegation of authority or organization.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in ACC 3210 or ACC 307.

courses.title: Business Valuation Using Financial Statements
courses.description: Cross Listed as: GBA 6000 Provides a framework for business analysis and valuation using financial statement data and gives practical advice when using the framework to value a firm. Emphasizes integration of key concepts from accounting finance, economic and business strategy and illustrates the latest techniques and information sources used by financial information industry professionals.

courses.title: Internal Control and Corporate Governance
courses.description: Cross Listed as: GBA 6100 Foundations of internal control theory accepted and promulgated by auditors and accountants. Management implementation of effective corporate governance. Best practices, benchmarks and models for evaluating and strengthening internal control and corporate governance.

courses.title: Assurance of Accounting Information Systems and Controls
courses.description: Applied perspective of Assurance of Accounting Information Systems (AIS) and Accounting Controls, providing students with comprehensive knowledge and skills necessary to assess and ensure the reliability, security, and integrity of financial information within organizations. Emphasizing theoretical foundations with practical applications, equipping students with a robust understanding of auditing principles, techniques, and methodologies as they pertain to AIS and controls.
courses.prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the MSA program.

courses.title: Assurance and Regulation in Accounting
courses.description: A managerial perspective on accounting assurance and regulatory requirements for all types of businesses. Emphasis on financial statement audits, public company requirements, other governmental regulation and internal auditing. Seminar course with problem solving and case studies.

courses.title: International Accounting Issues
courses.description: Exploration of international accounting issues from interdisciplinary, managerial perspectives. Comparative accounting across national borders. Harmonization and evaluation of international accounting standards. Foreign exchange. Mergers, acquisitions and business valuation. Ethics. Management control issues in international contexts.

courses.title: Management Accounting Seminar
courses.description: Strategic management accounting and control issues, including cost determination and analysis, activity-based systems, budgeting, transfer pricing, performance evaluation, cost management and ethics.

courses.title: Advanced Analytics in Accounting
courses.description: Advanced data analytics techniques used by accountants for decision making and the examination of “big data.” Development of data analytics skills through hands-on work with various software tools used by accounting professionals.

courses.title: Cybersecurity in Accounting
courses.description: Technology continues to evolve, and audit techniques need to evolve as well. An understanding of the cybersecurity threats to accounting information systems with an auditing perspective. Cybersecurity issues and challenges in accounting, network devices, servers, databases and other devices used in an accounting system, as well as techniques to audit and secure these systems. Corequisite(s): Unconditional admission to the MSA program.

courses.title: Contemporary Accounting Issues
courses.description: Study and analysis of contemporary accounting issues and practices. Emphasis on the integration of accounting knowledge in financial and managerial accounting, tax, accounting information systems, and auditing. Enhances analytical research, judgmental and communication skills of students.

courses.title: Management Control in Not-for-Profit Entities
courses.description: Financial issues faced by not-for-profit organizations. Budgeting, preparing for financial statements and required tax forms, financing, investing, internal control problems, auditing and analyzing financial statements of not-for-profit organizations including hospitals, educational institutions and charitable foundations.

courses.title: Fraud and Forensic Accounting
courses.description: Cross Listed as: GBA 6800 A managerial perspective on fraud within an organization. Emphasis on fraud prevention and detection methods. Survey of the management support resources available in the field of forensic accounting. Case study and analysis of financial statement frauds.

courses.title: Strategic Tax Planning
courses.description: Cross Listed as: GBA 6900 A hands-on course for Masters of Accountancy students on how to factor taxes into strategic decision-making. Course enables students to recognize and understand the impact of taxation as a major factor in business planning.

Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: MSA Research Project
courses.description: A written research project concerning a significant problem in the field of accounting.

courses.title: Master’s Project
courses.description: A written research project concerning a significant problem in the field of accounting.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of all MSA core courses. Advancement to candidacy.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.
